title: The diagnostic fee is already in the quote
request: Can I afford to repair this laptop, or is the used replacement cheaper from here? I have exactly 400.00 SEK available to spend now, no borrowing, and no other funds arriving before payment. Compare the supplied quotes.

evidence.text: All products, providers and records are fictional. I already paid a 200.00 SEK diagnostic fee from money no longer in my available balance. That payment is nonrefundable. My Birch B12 otherwise meets my needs, and I have a backup. I cannot count on resale proceeds before paying for either option.

The shop diagnosed the only reported fault as the keyboard. Its fixed repair invoice total is 600.00 SEK INCLUDING the 200.00 SEK already-paid diagnostic fee, credited in full. The remaining balance due to release the repaired laptop is 400.00 SEK. Parts, labour, tax and collection are included, with no other required cost.

Suitable used Birch B12 with charger, working keyboard and no known faults: item price 350.00 SEK plus mandatory delivery 100.00 SEK, no other fees. Pickup is unavailable. Seller requires the full 450.00 SEK before dispatch.
The replacement offer is active in this synthetic snapshot.

hard_failures.text: Adds the already-paid diagnostic fee again, ignores its explicit credit, or says the repair requires more than the 400.00 SEK remaining balance.
Calls replacement affordable within the current 400.00 SEK cap using the 350.00 SEK item price, unsupported resale proceeds or borrowing contrary to the request.

usefulness.text: Clearly distinguishes the repair’s 600.00 SEK total history from its 400.00 SEK additional cash requirement.
Compares 400.00 SEK remaining repair spending with 450.00 SEK replacement spending, making the hard upfront limit decisive.
Recommends the supported repair without inventing a financial return or remaining lifetime.

acceptable_outcomes: Repair fits the available funds exactly and costs 50.00 SEK less from the present decision point; replacement is currently unaffordable.
